Restricted temporal regression (RTR)

Source: R/temporal_rtr_posteriors.R
temporal_rtr.Rd

The temporal analogue of spatial_rsr(): constrain a temporal random effect to be orthogonal to a set of covariates, so a covariate that moves with the temporal trend does not share its signal with the temporal field, \(u_{RTR} = (I - P_X) u\).

Usage

temporal_rtr(temporal, restrict_to)

# S3 method for class 'tulpa_rtr'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

temporal

A single-walk temporal field: temporal_rw1(), temporal_rw2() (cyclic or not) or temporal_ar1(), without a group_var. The projection is applied by nested Laplace, which reads the field through a projector in place of its time index; a grouped (panel) walk, temporal_multiscale(), temporal_gp() and temporal_tvc() are not carried by that path and are refused here rather than accepted and then fitted unrestricted.

restrict_to

A one-sided formula giving the covariate space the temporal effect is made orthogonal to, e.g. ~ x.

x

A tulpa_rtr specification.

...

Passed to the print method of the restricted field.

Value

The temporal specification, flagged as restricted (class tulpa_rtr in front of its own classes). It keeps its type, so it validates against the data as the field it is.

Details

The projector is built at the field's own resolution: one row per time point, with the restricted design averaged over the observations at each, \(P_\perp = I - Q Q'\) with \(Q\) an orthonormal basis of that design. Observation \(i\) at time \(t_i\) receives \((P_\perp u)_{t_i}\), so the field reaches the linear predictor through \(S P_\perp\), \(S\) the observation-to-time incidence. A design that carries an intercept annihilates the field's constant, so an RW1 / RW2 walk's level reaches the predictor through the intercept alone.

What RTR estimates. As for spatial_rsr(), the restriction puts no part of the shared temporal signal in the field, so the fixed effect takes all of it: RTR targets the MARGINAL association between the covariate and the response, where the unrestricted temporal model targets the association conditional on the field. The two differ by exactly the covariate's projection onto the field, so they are different estimands rather than a biased and an unbiased version of one (Bradley, 2024). Measured on a confounded Gaussian fixture (5 seeds, 50 time points with 4 observations each, conditional slope 1.0, marginal slope 1.51 on average): the restricted fit averaged 0.018 from the marginal value and 0.51 from the conditional one under each of RW1, RW2 and AR1, the unrestricted fit 0.45 and 0.06 to 0.08.

The restriction is not free. For the spatial restriction Hanks et al. (2015) and Khan and Calder (2022) measured POORER interval coverage than under the model that does not restrict; that has not been measured here for a temporal field. Read an RTR interval as an interval for the marginal association under a correctly specified model.

A non-cyclic RW2 walk leaves its linear trend unpenalised; a restrict_to that spans the linear time trend (e.g. ~ x + year) would leave that direction identified by neither the prior nor the data, and the fit refuses it.

A restricted field is fitted by nested Laplace (mode = "auto", "structured" or "nested_laplace") under any family that path takes, on its own or alongside an areal or NNGP spatial field, smoothers, random effects or latent() blocks. temporal() reports the restricted field \(P_\perp u\), the quantity that enters the linear predictor.

References

Hodges, J. S., & Reich, B. J. (2010). Adding spatially-correlated errors can mess up the fixed effect you love. The American Statistician, 64(4), 325-334.

Hanks, E. M., Schliep, E. M., Hooten, M. B., & Hoeting, J. A. (2015). Restricted spatial regression in practice: geostatistical models, confounding, and robustness under model misspecification. Environmetrics, 26(4), 243-254.

Khan, K., & Calder, C. A. (2022). Restricted spatial regression methods: implications for inference. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 117(537), 482-494.

Bradley, J. R. (2024). Restricted spatial regression is reasonable statistical practice: clarifications, interpretations, and new developments. arXiv:2408.05106.

See also

spatial_rsr(), temporal_rw1(), temporal_rw2(), temporal_ar1()

Examples

temporal_rtr(temporal_rw1("year"), restrict_to = ~ x)
#> tulpa temporal specification
#> ============================
#> 
#> Type: RW1 (First-order Random Walk) 
#> Time variable: year 
#> Shared: Yes (enters both processes) 
#> 
#> Restricted Temporal Regression (RTR):
#>   Orthogonal to: ~x 

# \donttest{
set.seed(2)
n_t <- 40
trend <- as.numeric(arima.sim(list(ar = 0.9), n_t, sd = 0.3))
df <- data.frame(year = rep(seq_len(n_t), each = 3))
df$x <- trend[df$year] + rnorm(nrow(df), 0, 0.3)
df$y <- rnorm(nrow(df), 1 + df$x + trend[df$year], 0.3)
fit <- tulpa(y ~ x, data = df, family = "gaussian",
             temporal = temporal_rtr(temporal_ar1("year"), ~ x))
#> Warning: NaNs produced
coef(fit)
#> (Intercept)           x 
#>   0.9717938   1.7874263 
# }
